changes.summary: Rosters now open in your team's colours, with your last result, next game and season so far — every dot opens that week on the schedule.
changes.headline: Rosters open in your team's colours
changes.lede: The roster page leads with your club now — its colour, its crest, your record, rank and points — then last week's result, this week's game and every week of the season as a row you can click straight into the schedule. One header, both leagues.
changes.imageAlt: TheLeague's roster page with the new header: the club nameplate in its own colour, last result and next game, the season rail, and every club's crest in a row below

changes.summary: The roster header's cap space now includes dead money and updates as you simulate cuts, trades and extensions.
Free Agents now shows a lock next to recently dropped players MFL won't let you add yet, and claiming one explains why instead of failing with HTTP 502.
When a waiver claim or first-come add fails, the claim window now shows MFL's reason and a link to its add/drop page instead of a bare HTTP error.
Live Scoring's win-probability bar now reads in the same order as the scoreboard: the team on the left gets the left share of the bar, in its own colour.
Live Scoring: an open matchup has breathing room below the Week dropdown again, and no longer shows the "updated" status twice.
MFL Live sign-in at v2.mfl.football/login now works for every league's owners, not just TheLeague's, so AFL owners can watch all their teams on one board.
MFL Live league boards show each outside league's own uploaded team logos again, and only fall back to NFL logos in a league that has none.
MFL Live's Top Performances lists each player once, with everyone who started him on a second line, instead of repeating the player for every owner.
MFL Live's league standings now update live by default, re-ranking as scores change, with Projected and Final views one tap away.
MFL Live's Live standings no longer add a 0-0 tie before kickoff when a starting lineup includes a player on bye.
Throwback Week: Cowboy Up now suits up as the Degenerates, a one-time commissioner exception borrowed from Da Dangsters' 2008-2014 era.
Throwback Week: standings now show each team's old-school art, with today's team name on a second line underneath.
Throwback era picker: a borrowed era now reads "on loan from Da Dangsters" instead of claiming your team once wore it under another franchise slot.
Throwback Week: claim any era from an owner who has left the league — first come, first served, one team per look. Your own eras stay yours, and so does your default until you pick another.
